title: Cost-Sharing Cap Percent for Low-Income Households
content:
**Rate schedule — cost-sharing cap percent, Medicaid Managed Care Membership**

The cap percent on which a member's cost-sharing cap is figured follows household income and ongoing authorized care. A household at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty level whose member holds at least one authorization approved on a request received in the counting window takes a cap percent of 2.5; a household at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty level whose member holds no such approved authorization takes a cap percent of 4.0; any other household keeps the category's cap percent.

## Terms used in this schedule

- **Household income.** The household income on file on the membership, as a whole percent of the federal poverty level.
- **Approved authorization.** An authorization on the member's Prior Authorization records that stands approved and whose request received date falls in the counting window. The count reads the Prior Authorization records' status and received date.
- **Counting window.** The number of months in the category's cap period counted back from the review date, a date counting when it lies fewer than that many whole months before the review date.

## Schedule

| Household income on file | Approved authorization on a request received in the counting window | Cap percent |
|---|---|---|
| At or below 185 percent of the federal poverty level | At least one | 2.5 |
| At or below 185 percent of the federal poverty level | None | 4.0 |
| Above 185 percent of the federal poverty level | Either | The category's cap percent |

## Band boundary

The band top of 185 percent is inclusive. A household on file at 185 percent is inside the low-income band; a household on file at 186 percent is above it and keeps the category's cap percent whatever its authorizations show.

## Hypothetical readings

The following cases use invented facts for illustration only.

- Income on file at 150 percent; the Prior Authorization records show one authorization approved on a request received inside the counting window. Cap percent: 2.5.
- Income on file at 185 percent; the only approved authorization was requested before the counting window began. No approved authorization counts, so the cap percent is 4.0.
- Income on file at 210 percent; two approved authorizations in the window. The household is above 185 percent, so the category's cap percent applies.
- Income on file at 120 percent; an authorization requested inside the window was denied. A denied authorization is not an approved one, so the cap percent is 4.0.
